_meta.note: Wealth figures: AFR Rich List 2026 (published 28 May 2026; manual update each May). Entries marked wealth_year 2025 have not yet been re-checked against the 2026 list. Political donations: AEC annual returns. NHMRC/ARC: budget papers. Charitable giving: individual figures removed because no verifiable source was found (the AFR Philanthropy 50 lists foundations, not these individuals' totals).

_stats.abs_median_salary_note: ABS Average Weekly Earnings May 2026 — full-time adult AVERAGE (mean) weekly ordinary time earnings, $2,083.70 × 52. NB: this is the mean, not the median (the median is lower).
_stats.au_population_note: ABS National, state and territory population (approx. 27.4M, 2025)
_stats.au_students_note: ACARA 2024 — total enrolments primary + secondary government and non-government schools
_stats.fossil_fuel_subsidies_note: Australia Institute, Fossil fuel subsidies in Australia 2026 — $16.3B in 2025-26 (federal + state), up 9.4% on 2024-25.
_stats.nhmrc_budget_note: NHMRC Medical Research Endowment Account grants, 2026-27 Budget (Health PBS 2026-27: $1,058.8M)
_stats.mrff_budget_note: MRFF disbursements base of $650M a year (capped since 2018-19); 2026-27 Budget adds $508.5M over 4 years, rising to $1B a year by 2030-31
_stats.housing_waitlist_note: AIHW Housing assistance in Australia 2026 — 206,000 households on the consolidated social housing waitlist at June 2025

billionaires.name: Gina Rinehart
billionaires.wealth_note: Entirely private company — no listed price to track. Manual update required.
billionaires.assetNote: Wealth is mostly in Hancock Prospecting Pty Ltd — a private, unlisted company built on Pilbara iron ore.
billionaires.inherited: Inherited Hancock Prospecting and its iron-ore royalty interests from her father Lang Hancock in 1992; has since expanded it greatly (notably the Roy Hill mine).

billionaires.name: Harry Triguboff
billionaires.wealth_note: Private company (Meriton). No listed price. Manual update required.
billionaires.assetNote: Meriton holds a vast rental apartment portfolio in addition to development pipeline. Sydney-centric with QLD presence.
billionaires.inherited: Self-made. Born in China; came to Australia as a teenager and founded Meriton in 1963.

billionaires.name: Anthony Pratt & family
billionaires.wealth_note: Private company (Visy/Pratt Industries). No listed price. Manual update required.
billionaires.donate: Pratt Philanthropies — AFR Philanthropy 50 (2025 list, FY2024 giving)
billionaires.assetNote: Visy (AU/NZ) and Pratt Industries (USA) are both private packaging and recycling empires.
billionaires.inherited: Inherited. Visy was started in Melbourne in 1948 by partners including Richard Pratt's father, Leon; Richard ran it from 1969 and built it into a global group, and Anthony took over as executive chairman after Richard's death in 2009.

billionaires.name: Clive Palmer
billionaires.wealth_note: Private company (Mineralogy). No listed price. Manual update required.
billionaires.polDonate: $52.9M Trumpet of Patriots + $0.3M UAP, via Mineralogy (2024–25)
billionaires.assetNote: Mineralogy controls iron ore royalties in the Pilbara. Palmer also holds significant hotel and property assets.
billionaires.inherited: Self-made: early wealth from Gold Coast property in the 1980s, then mining royalties (Mineralogy) and long legal battles.

billionaires.name: Melanie Perkins & Obrecht
billionaires.wealth_note: Private company (Canva). No listed price. Manual update required when Canva IPOs.
billionaires.polDonate: None found in reporting on 2024–25 AEC returns
billionaires.assetNote: Canva remains private, so its value comes from private funding rounds and share sales. An IPO or sale of shares would crystallise gains.
billionaires.inherited: Self-made. Started Fusion Books in Perth, then co-founded Canva in Sydney in 2012 with Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams.

billionaires.name: Michael Dorrell
billionaires.wealth_note: Private firm (Stonepeak). No listed price. Manual update required.
billionaires.polDonate: None found in reporting on 2024–25 AEC returns
billionaires.assetNote: Stonepeak is a global alternative investment firm focused on infrastructure assets. Dorrell is founding partner.
billionaires.inherited: Self-made. Co-founded Stonepeak in 2011 after a career at Blackstone.

billionaires.name: Kerry Stokes
billionaires.wealth_note: ~58% wealth in Seven Group Holdings (SVW.AX). Auto-updated daily from ASX price. AFR 2025 figure — not in the 2026 top 10; re-check against the 2026 list.
billionaires.polDonate: $200k Australian Capital Equity → WA Labor (2024–25, as reported; check AEC register)
billionaires.assetNote: Seven Group Holdings (SVW) is publicly listed. Stokes also holds direct property, art, and media assets.
billionaires.inherited: Self-made. Born in Melbourne in 1940 and raised in poverty; built a media and industrial group in Western Australia.

billionaires.name: Scott Farquhar
billionaires.wealth_note: AFR Rich List 2026 (with Kim Jackson): fell from $21.4B to $11.7B as Atlassian shares fell.
billionaires.polDonate: None found in reporting on 2024–25 AEC returns
billionaires.assetNote: Wealth is almost entirely in publicly listed Atlassian Corporation. High volatility with stock price.
billionaires.inherited: Self-made. Co-founded Atlassian in 2002 with Mike Cannon-Brookes.
